scope: atlas-backed gross anatomy, labels and terminology prepared for future clinical sign-off
unresolvedLimitations: Independent medical review of the complete atlas label set and Japanese terminology is not yet recorded.
Imaging-atlas-derived deep structures are approximate and are not asserted at voxel-level or patient-specific resolution.
Functional summaries are orientation notes only and must not be read as one-to-one functional localisation.
The scene must not be used for diagnosis, lesion localisation, stereotactic coordinates, operative planning or navigation.

scope: candidate-asset gross anatomy: fourteen named parts of one reference heart, prepared for future clinical sign-off
unresolvedLimitations: No anatomist and no clinician has reviewed this geometry, its labels or the Japanese terminology.
The great vessels — aorta, pulmonary trunk, superior and inferior vena cava, pulmonary veins — are absent from the source file, so this is not a complete gross anatomy of the heart.
The chamber meshes enclose the chambers' spaces; the file contains no myocardial free wall, so no wall thickness, no endocardial surface and no interior view is offered or implied.
The enclosed volumes recorded in the adapter are properties of one fixed cadaveric specimen and are not chamber volumes, end-diastolic volumes or any other clinical measurement.
The source file is a candidate under examination: its licences (HuBMAP CC BY 4.0; NLM Visible Human terms) are recorded and not discharged, and it has passed no asset release gate.
The scene must not be used for diagnosis, treatment selection, dose selection, prognosis or procedure planning.

scope: steady-state haemodynamic model, calculated global oxygen delivery and teaching presentation prepared for future clinical sign-off
unresolvedLimitations: The scene is one constructed low-flow teaching case and is not a patient simulator, resuscitation protocol, fluid challenge or dose-response model.
The model is steady-state and omits pulsatility, vascular compliance, wave reflection, filling pressures, congestion and treatment interactions.
Arterial oxygen content is fixed, so haemodilution, gas-exchange change, microcirculation, extraction, oxygen consumption and lactate are outside the model.
The fluid and dobutamine response magnitudes are illustrative and cannot predict whether or how strongly an individual patient will respond.
MAP and calculated global oxygen delivery do not establish adequate tissue or organ perfusion.

reviewerRole: historical review role not recorded under the current registry standard
scope: current model card, evidence dossier and external-biology test layer prepared; historical clinical sign-off remains unversioned
unresolvedLimitations: No versioned clinical attestation exists under the current review standard.
The progression axis is a conceptual aggregation state, not clinical stage, symptom severity, or elapsed disease time.
Aβ40 and Aβ42, tau pathology, neuroinflammation, APP processing, ApoE and patient-level cognition are outside the model.
Particle counts, molecular scale and aggregation thresholds are illustrative rather than measured quantities.
Individual rendered particles move only forward on the teaching slider even though real Aβ assemblies can interconvert and disassemble.

reviewerRole: historical review role not recorded under the current registry standard
scope: current model card, evidence dossier and external-physiology test layer prepared; historical clinical sign-off remains unversioned
unresolvedLimitations: No versioned clinical attestation exists under the current review standard.
The scene represents one illustrative HFrEF remodelling pattern and is not a universal natural history of heart failure.
HFpEF, valvular disease, right-heart failure, pulmonary hypertension, neurohumoral regulation and distributed vascular wave mechanics are outside the model.
The valves are ideal one-way resistances and several pressure-volume parameters are calibrated educational values rather than patient measurements.
The visible congestion map is a teaching transform of solved pressure rather than a lung-water model or individual oedema threshold.

unresolvedLimitations: The equal-pressure-point flow envelope underestimates maximal flow near TLC and must not be read as peak expiratory flow.
The model does not represent gas exchange, PaO2, PaCO2 or oxygen saturation.
Breathing pattern is prescribed rather than selected by the patient/model, and compliance is simplified.
The model cannot reproduce worsening gas trapping caused by dynamic airway compression during forceful expiration.

airway anatomy and causal claims
scene read-outs and public teaching copy
model card, evidence dossier and documented limitations
unresolvedLimitations: Poiseuille scaling is used only as a relative approximation across an idealised airway tree.
The tree is symmetric and truncated to eight generations; spatial adjacency is tree adjacency rather than real three-dimensional lung anatomy.
The equilibrium model contains no bronchoconstriction time course or gas exchange.
The lung-inflation control represents parenchymal tethering only and must not be interpreted as the clinical bronchodilator response to a deep inspiration.

scope: core portal-haemodynamic network
causal ordering and HVPG interpretation
scene read-outs and public teaching copy
model card, evidence dossier and documented limitations
unresolvedLimitations: The model is an equilibrium network and does not represent the time course of collateral formation or disease progression.
Collateral recruitment is an illustrative smooth mapping rather than a physiological valve or clinical threshold law.
WHVP is treated as equal to sinusoidal pressure by construction although clinically it is an approximation.
Prehepatic portal vein thrombosis, ascites, bleeding, encephalopathy and liver function are outside the model.

scope: series-path model of mechanical bowel obstruction, prepared for future clinical sign-off: what the site of a blockage decides about the bowel above and below it
unresolvedLimitations: The lengths and calibres are the intestinal atlas's drawn proportions, not anatomical ones. What is claimed is the ordering — that the caecum is the widest part of the large bowel — and not the ratios.

The wall tension figure is an index rather than a tension or a pressure. It compares segments inside one picture; comparing the number between two scenarios is not something the model supports, and no value in it is a threshold.
There is no time and no rate anywhere in the model. The axis is how completely the path is blocked, not how long it has been blocked, and nothing in it is hours.
There is no ischaemia, no strangulation, no perforation and no risk of any of them, no cause, no fluid shift and no treatment. Symptoms are outside the model entirely.
The drawn gut ends at the sigmoid: there is no rectum and no anal canal, so a blockage there has nothing below it on screen.

scope: swallow-transport model of failed sphincter relaxation and failed peristalsis, prepared for future clinical sign-off: where what was swallowed ends up, and what settles the answer
unresolvedLimitations: The conductance across the sphincter and the cross-section a retained column stands in are numbers this repository chose so that a normal swallow clears and a failed one balances inside a human oesophagus. They are not measurements and no figure is a threshold.
Nothing here is manometry. No value the model reports is an integrated relaxation pressure, a classification subtype or a measured tracing, and the model identifies no cause.
The axis moves the two failures together because one loss produces both. In a person they do not move in step, and the model has no time in it to move them through.

The mapping from the axis to the two parameters is deliberately non-linear so the band in which a column can still balance a swallow is visible. A reviewer should check that the stages land where the copy says they do.

scope: geometric model of hip osteoarthritis by direction of joint space loss, prepared for future clinical sign-off: what is left of the layer round the socket and how far the two centres have come apart
unresolvedLimitations: The fractions reported are of a layer this repository drew and are not joint space widths. Joint space width is millimetres between bone surfaces on a weight-bearing radiograph in a direction somebody chose; nothing here is measured, weight-bearing or millimetres.
There is no pain, stiffness, limp, range or anything a person can do anywhere in the model, and nothing in it makes any of them follow from how much layer is left.
There is no loading in the model at all, so the loop by which where the ball sits changes what it loads is left open rather than represented.
Four patterns stand for a continuum of directions, and the space is drawn as a ring in one plane. A hip is not a disc.
Cysts, sclerosis, osteophytes, dysplasia, impingement, avascular necrosis, every grading system and every treatment are outside the model, as are time, progression and cause.

scope: geometric model of a supraspinatus tear, prepared for future clinical sign-off: what is left holding the humeral head on its socket and whether that keeps it centred
unresolvedLimitations: The rise is a fraction of the shoulder atlas's subacromial display gap, which the atlas declares to be a value opened up so the tendon could be seen. It is not an acromiohumeral distance and it is not millimetres.
The facing pair is one number rather than two tendons. Which of them is involved, and how far round, is not represented.
Nothing in the model moves an arm. There is no pain, no weakness, no arc of movement and no range anywhere in it.
Impingement as a syndrome, the bursa, tendinopathy, calcium, retraction, muscle quality and cuff tear arthropathy are all outside the model, as are cause, time, healing and every treatment.
The tendons the scene does not redraw stay where the atlas put them while the head moves: they are context and are not re-solved.

scope: geometric model of an anterior cruciate ligament injury, prepared for future clinical sign-off: the ligament's own state and what is left restraining the tibia
unresolvedLimitations: Nothing in the model is a Lachman test, an anterior drawer or a pivot shift. Those are manoeuvres a person performs and grade by what they feel; there is no examiner in this model and nothing in the scene is being tested.
The distance reported is a fraction of a tibial plateau this repository drew. It is not millimetres and not a side-to-side difference.
How the restraint divides between the ligament and everything else is this repository's reading of the word primary. The model claims the ordering and never the split.
The collateral ligaments and the tendon across the front are context and are not re-solved when the tibia moves; only the two cruciates follow it.
There is no mechanism of injury, no pain, no swelling, no giving way, no rotation, no healing and no treatment anywhere in the model.

scope: geometric model of compartmental knee osteoarthritis, prepared for future clinical sign-off: what is left of the layer on each side and what follows on the side that lost it
unresolvedLimitations: The fraction the model reports is of its own drawn layer and is not a joint space width. Joint space width is millimetres between bone surfaces on a weight-bearing radiograph and includes the meniscus; nothing here is measured, weight-bearing or millimetres.
There is no pain, stiffness, function or anything a person can do anywhere in the model, and nothing in it makes any of them follow from how much layer is left.
There is no loading in the model at all, so the loop by which uneven loss loads the worn side harder is left open rather than represented.
The joint is drawn in extension and nothing in the scene moves; a knee's compartments load differently through the range and none of that is here.
Marginal bone is drawn as a swelling of the rim. Where osteophytes grow, in what shape and in what order is not in the model, and no size on screen is a grade.

scope: geometric model of an enlarging nodular thyroid by direction, prepared for future clinical sign-off: whether the airway is displaced or narrowed, and what the gland reaches behind it
unresolvedLimitations: There is no thyroid function of any kind in the model. A goitre of any shape here may be euthyroid, overactive or underactive, and nothing about the shape says which; the scene exists partly to refuse that inference.

Nothing in this model is a measurement. The lobe's volume and depth and the airway's calibre are measured off the thyroid atlas, whose own proportions are drawn to be legible, and the width across the airway is reported against the model's own resting width rather than as a tracheal diameter.
The nerve and parathyroid relation is anatomy and not injury. Nothing in the model says a nerve is damaged or at risk, or that a parathyroid gland has stopped working.
The four directions and how much of each meets a boundary are this repository's reading of four standard pictures. A real goitre goes several ways at once and the four are not exclusive.
The thoracic inlet is a structure the scene adds, because the atlas has no skeleton. There is no malignancy, no cytology, no symptom, no time and no treatment anywhere in the model.

scope: geometric model of one uterine fibroid by location in the wall, prepared for future clinical sign-off: what the depth at which it sits decides
unresolvedLimitations: Nothing in this model is a measurement. The wall's depth, the cavity's area and the organ's volume are measured off the uterine atlas, whose own proportions are drawn to be legible rather than to scale, and no centimetre or millilitre follows from any of it.

Bleeding, pain, pressure symptoms, fertility and pregnancy are outside the model entirely, and nothing in it makes any of them follow from size. That they do not follow from size in any simple way is why the scene is about location.
The uterus is not redrawn around the fibroid: the model has no tissue mechanics and does not work out how an organ takes the shape of what is inside it.

The three depths are this repository's reading of three standard names, and the boundaries between those names are not sharp. There is exactly one fibroid, and most uteruses that have them have several.
There is no time, no growth, no hormone, no degeneration, no sarcoma and no treatment anywhere in the model.

scope: geometric zonal model of benign prostatic enlargement, prepared for future clinical sign-off: which zone enlarges, and what that does to the zones that do not
unresolvedLimitations: Nothing in this model is a measurement. The proportions are the prostate atlas's display proportions, drawn so four zones can be told apart rather than to scale, and no volume may be read off them.

The channel is reported as a fraction of this model's own resting lumen and is not a calibre. How much it narrows per unit of transition-zone growth is an assumed relation: the model has no tissue mechanics and cannot derive it.
There is no urine, no flow, no flow rate, no post-void residual, no bladder wall, no detrusor, no symptom and no score anywhere in the model, and no figure in it is a threshold.
Lateral-lobe and median-lobe patterns are offered as two described arrangements. Which one a gland takes is not something a volume can tell you, and the control is a shape rather than a severity.

scope: four-resistance duct model of biliary outflow, prepared for future clinical sign-off: which segments a blockage at a named site puts behind it, and which it leaves alone
unresolvedLimitations: The resistances are calibration constants chosen to put an unobstructed common bile duct near ten centimetres of water at an ordinary bile flow. They are not measurements, and no figure in the model is a threshold.
The model carries no bilirubin, jaundice, pain, inflammation, infection, stone or enzyme, and no diagnosis follows from it. Cholecystitis, cholangitis and pancreatitis are named nowhere in it.
Every state is an equilibrium. The model cannot show a duct dilating over days or a gallbladder filling over hours; its only time is the cystic duct's time constant, which is a ratio.
A common channel at the papilla is one of several anatomical arrangements. Where the two ducts open separately, the ampullary case does not behave as this model shows.

scope: model and evidence package prepared for future clinical sign-off
unresolvedLimitations: The model intentionally isolates haemodynamic and neurohumoral mechanisms and contains no structural kidney injury.
There is no tubule, sodium handling, urine output, ascites, hyponatraemia or differential diagnosis of AKI.
Treatment controls show mechanistic direction only and do not represent dose, response rate, adverse effects or a complete terlipressin treatment model.
Cardiac compensation, vasoconstrictor activation and several treatment gains are illustrative parameterisations.

scope: glomerular Starling balance, tubular sodium/urea/water/albumin mass balance and the derived bedside indices, prepared for future clinical sign-off
unresolvedLimitations: The model solves a steady state. Plasma creatinine is reported as where creatinine is heading at the current filtration rate, never as a value measurable today, and whether that caveat is stated strongly enough for the audience the scene reaches has not been reviewed.

FENa, the fractional excretion of urea and the urea-to-creatinine ratio are reproduced in direction but must not be read as predicting that a patient crosses the 1% or 20:1 line. Whether presenting them at all risks being read as a diagnostic algorithm has not been reviewed.
The chronic sodium adaptation term lumps increased solute load per nephron and natriuretic factors into one bounded expression and is the least directly sourced part of the model.
Backleak of filtrate across damaged tubular epithelium is an accepted third mechanism of the low GFR in acute tubular injury and is not modelled.

Acid-base, potassium, phosphate, calcium, vitamin D and erythropoietin are absent, as is anything outside the kidney; aldosterone and antidiuretic hormone are inputs standing in for a body that is not modelled.

Several exponents (glomerulotubular balance, urea handling, remnant hyperfiltration, tubular injury feedback) are calibration constants chosen so the reference kidney lands on textbook values; only the sign and the reason for each effect is asserted.

scope: the Starling balance across the pulmonary capillary, the three buffers that oppose it, the staging of interstitial before alveolar filling and the shunt derived from the flooded fraction, prepared for future clinical sign-off
unresolvedLimitations: The model has no gravitational gradient, so it fills the lung evenly where real oedema is basal. Whether a scene that draws an even distribution can teach the staging without teaching the wrong distribution has not been reviewed.

The model has no ventilation, no respiratory rate and no carbon dioxide, so it cannot produce the symptom this disease presents with. Whether presenting oedema primarily as an oxygenation problem misleads has not been reviewed.

The scene reports a specific flooding threshold in mmHg for the reference lung. It is searched for rather than stored and moves with every control, but whether reporting it as a number at all invites it being read as a clinical threshold has not been reviewed.

scope: coronary territory anatomy, the accumulation of ischemic burden, and its regional and global mechanical consequences
unresolvedLimitations: Independent medical review of the ischemia calibration and of the teaching text is not recorded.

The coronary territory map is the AHA fixed assignment, which measurement disagrees with in places — segment 3 is charted to the right coronary and measures as anterior-descending territory, and five further segments overlap two arteries between people.
One right-dominant specimen. Left-dominant and balanced circulations are not modelled.
Supply is a scale factor on a territory and not a stenosis: there is no flow calculation and no relationship here between a lumen and a flow reserve.
The time axis is normalized episode progress and not minutes. No claim is made about how long ischemia takes to develop or to recover.
Reversible ischemia only. No infarction, necrosis, scar or infarct expansion; no ECG, chest pain, troponin or prognosis.
The scene must not be used to assess a person's coronary anatomy, to judge whether someone is having a heart attack, or to infer treatment.

scope: regional ventilation-perfusion model of alveolar consolidation and intrapulmonary shunt, prepared for future clinical sign-off
unresolvedLimitations: The twelve equal regional units and their clustered ordering are illustrative and do not reproduce lobar, segmental, bronchopneumonic or imaging distributions.
The model represents alveolar consolidation only and contains no pathogen, immune response, respiratory mechanics, PaO2, SpO2, carbon dioxide or treatment response.
Hypoxic pulmonary vasoconstriction is one bounded diversion scalar and has no patient-level calibration; the displayed shunt is a model fraction, not a clinical shunt measurement.

scope: parallel-territory model of pulmonary vascular obstruction, underperfused ventilation and relative vascular load, prepared for future clinical sign-off
unresolvedLimitations: The twelve equal parallel vascular territories, fixed driving pressure and obstruction ordering are illustrative and do not reproduce pulmonary arterial anatomy or CT clot burden.
The model contains no changing cardiac output, vasoactive response, vascular recruitment, RV geometry, RV-pulmonary artery coupling, oxygenation, carbon dioxide, infarction or treatment.
The underperfused-ventilation and relative-resistance outputs are model indices, not VD/VT, measured PVR, pulmonary artery pressure, RV function, clinical category or risk score.

scope: procedurally built gross anatomy, bilingual labels and selection behaviour prepared for future clinical sign-off
unresolvedLimitations: Independent medical review of the label set and the Japanese terminology is not yet recorded.
Airway calibres, lengths and branching angles are drawn to read clearly and are not measured; the right-to-left main bronchus difference is understated.
Bronchopulmonary segment boundaries are the definition applied (the lung nearest one segmental bronchus) rather than a specimen traced, so they are smooth where real ones are not.
No pleura, lymphatics, bronchial circulation or alveoli are modelled, and nothing in the scene is solved.
The scene must not be used for diagnosis, treatment or dose selection, prognosis, or planning bronchoscopy, biopsy, resection or localisation.

scope: procedurally built Couinaud segmentation, bilingual labels and selection behaviour prepared for future clinical sign-off
unresolvedLimitations: Independent medical review of the label set and the Japanese terminology is not yet recorded.
The outer form is a warped ellipsoid with a liver's proportions: no porta hepatis notch, no bare area, no ligamentous attachments.
No biliary duct system and no hepatic artery are drawn, and the gallbladder carries no volume.
Segment volume shares are reference proportions used to check the partition, not a measurement of any individual liver.
The scene must not be used for diagnosis, treatment or dose selection, prognosis, or planning resection, donor evaluation, ablation or volumetry.

scope: procedurally built renal parenchyma and collecting system, bilingual labels and selection behaviour prepared for future clinical sign-off
unresolvedLimitations: Independent medical review of the label set and the Japanese terminology is not yet recorded.
No renal artery or vein is drawn at any level, so nothing vascular can be read from this scene.

Schematic where the model card says so: the renal sinus is not carved out, the seven pyramids are one coronal row rather than an anterior and a posterior one, and the corticomedullary junction is the capsule scaled rather than a surface of its own.
Only one kidney is partitioned; the other is a landmark shape declared as a single unpartitioned structure.
The ureter's calibre and course are illustrative and its three normal narrowings are not modelled.
The scene must not be used for diagnosis, treatment or dose selection, prognosis, or planning biopsy, nephrostomy, stone localisation or stenting.

scope: procedurally built gastric regions, bilingual labels and selection behaviour prepared for future clinical sign-off
unresolvedLimitations: Independent medical review of the label set and the Japanese terminology is not yet recorded.
The regions are drawn as rings of one tube: the cardia becomes a collar all the way round, and the incisura angularis is present only as the narrowing that goes with it.
No wall layers, rugae, gastric glands or volumes are modelled, and no gastric emptying occurs in this scene.
The scene must not be used for diagnosis, treatment or dose selection, prognosis, or planning endoscopy, biopsy or resection.

scope: procedurally built colonic parts, bilingual labels and selection behaviour prepared for future clinical sign-off
unresolvedLimitations: Independent medical review of the label set and the Japanese terminology is not yet recorded.
Lengths, loop counts and positions are illustrative; no dimension can be read from this model.
Jejunum and ileum are one structure because no boundary between them is modelled, and where the caecum ends is schematic because no ileum is drawn arriving.
No appendix, ileocaecal valve, rectum, anal canal, mesentery, taenia coli or wall layer is modelled.
The scene must not be used for diagnosis, treatment or dose selection, prognosis, or planning colonoscopy, resection or stoma siting.

scope: procedurally built pancreatic parts, duct and islets, bilingual labels and selection behaviour prepared for future clinical sign-off
unresolvedLimitations: Independent medical review of the label set and the Japanese terminology is not yet recorded.
Islet number and size are illustrative and stand for an arrangement, not a count: they must not be read as a quantity of endocrine tissue.
No uncinate process, accessory duct, common bile duct, ampulla or papilla is modelled, and no vessel is drawn.
Nothing is secreted or solved in this scene.
The scene must not be used for diagnosis, treatment or dose selection, prognosis, or planning ERCP, biopsy, resection or staging.

scope: procedurally built thyroid lobes, isthmus, pyramidal lobe, parathyroid glands and recurrent laryngeal nerves, bilingual labels and selection behaviour prepared for future clinical sign-off
unresolvedLimitations: Independent medical review of the label set and the Japanese terminology is not yet recorded.
Parathyroid positions are plausible rather than fixed, and four is the usual number rather than the only one: they must not be read as where to look.
The pyramidal lobe is drawn every time although it is present in roughly half of people.
The recurrent laryngeal nerves' course below the neck is not modelled, so the difference between the two sides is not shown.
No vessel, cartilage ring, strap muscle, fascia or lymph node is drawn, and nothing is secreted or solved in this scene.
The scene must not be used for diagnosis, treatment or dose selection, prognosis, or planning thyroidectomy, parathyroid exploration, nerve monitoring or biopsy.

scope: procedurally built splenic arterial segments and hilar vessels, bilingual labels and selection behaviour prepared for future clinical sign-off
unresolvedLimitations: Independent medical review of the label set and the Japanese terminology is not yet recorded.
The segment plane is flat and passes through the hilum; real boundaries are neither flat nor identical between people, and two segments is the usual number rather than the only one.
Red and white pulp are not drawn, and no capsule, trabecula or short gastric vessel is modelled.
Nothing flows or is solved in this scene.
The scene must not be used for diagnosis, treatment or dose selection, prognosis, or planning splenectomy, partial splenectomy or embolisation.

scope: procedurally built bladder wall parts, trigone and orifices, bilingual labels and selection behaviour prepared for future clinical sign-off
unresolvedLimitations: Independent medical review of the label set and the Japanese terminology is not yet recorded.
The trigone is a flat patch with no thickness, and the mucosal folds it is smooth by contrast with are not drawn.
The bladder is drawn at one fixed degree of filling; nothing fills or empties in this scene.
The ureters' oblique intramural course, the sphincters, the detrusor's layers and the urachal remnant are not modelled.
The urethra is drawn the same for everyone: male and female urethral anatomy differ and neither is represented.
The scene must not be used for diagnosis, treatment or dose selection, prognosis, or planning cystoscopy, catheterisation, resection or stenting.

scope: procedurally built gallbladder parts and bile-duct tree with its duodenal outlet, bilingual labels and selection behaviour prepared for future clinical sign-off
unresolvedLimitations: Independent medical review of the label set and the Japanese terminology is not yet recorded.
Calibres, lengths and angles are drawn to be legible; only the order of the junctions is claimed.
The liver is not drawn, so the hepatic ducts begin at the edge of the model.
The common bile duct runs in front of the duodenum and the pancreatic head rather than behind and through them.

The spiral valve, the sphincter of Oddi, Hartmann's pouch, the minor papilla and the common channel are not modelled, and the well-known variations in cystic and hepatic duct anatomy are drawn one way only.
The scene must not be used for diagnosis, treatment or dose selection, prognosis, or planning cholecystectomy, ERCP, stenting or any biliary procedure.

scope: procedurally built oesophageal parts, the three constrictions and the structures that make them, bilingual labels and selection behaviour prepared for future clinical sign-off
unresolvedLimitations: Independent medical review of the label set and the Japanese terminology is not yet recorded.
Lengths, calibres and angles are drawn to be legible; no distance from the incisors is given or implied, and none may be read off the model.
The middle constriction is drawn as one although it is often counted as two (aortic and bronchial).

Muscle layers, the upper and lower oesophageal sphincters, the diaphragmatic crura, the vagus nerves and the submucosal venous plexus are not drawn, so nothing here shows why reflux is resisted or how varices form.
The scene must not be used for diagnosis, treatment or dose selection, prognosis, or planning endoscopy, dilatation, stenting or any oesophageal procedure.

scope: procedurally built adrenal cortical zones and medulla on both sides, bilingual labels and selection behaviour prepared for future clinical sign-off
unresolvedLimitations: Independent medical review of the label set and the Japanese terminology is not yet recorded.
The zone thicknesses are drawn so that three zones can be told apart and are not the real proportions; only their order from the capsule inwards is claimed.
No capsule, vessel or nerve is drawn, and the medulla's chromaffin cells and their sympathetic supply are not represented.
Nothing is secreted or solved in this scene; the two time courses are `adrenal-response`.
The scene must not be used for diagnosis, treatment or dose selection, prognosis, or planning adrenalectomy, venous sampling or biopsy.

scope: procedurally built uterine parts, cavity and cervical canal, fallopian tubes and ovaries, bilingual labels and selection behaviour prepared for future clinical sign-off
unresolvedLimitations: Independent medical review of the label set and the Japanese terminology is not yet recorded.
The uterus is drawn upright rather than in its usual anteverted, anteflexed position.
The cavity is a flat patch with no thickness, and the endometrium lining it is not drawn as tissue.
Endometrium, myometrium and perimetrium are not separated, and nothing here changes with the cycle.
The fallopian tube is one structure with a changing calibre: its named lengths and the fimbriae are not separately selectable.
Follicles, corpora lutea, ligaments, fornices, the transformation zone and the vessels are not drawn.
The scene must not be used for diagnosis, treatment or dose selection, prognosis, or planning hysteroscopy, device insertion, surgery or any obstetric decision.

scope: procedurally built prostatic zones, urethra, ejaculatory ducts and seminal vesicles with their bladder and rectal relations, bilingual labels and selection behaviour prepared for future clinical sign-off
unresolvedLimitations: Independent medical review of the label set and the Japanese terminology is not yet recorded.
The zone proportions are drawn so four zones can be told apart and are not the real ones: no volume, ratio or zone size may be read off the model.
Zone boundaries are surfaces of revolution and planes; real ones are neither, and they vary between people and with age.
The capsule, the neurovascular bundles, the sphincters, the prostatic utricle, the periurethral glands and Denonvilliers' fascia are not drawn.
Benign enlargement and cancer are not represented in any form, and nothing here is anyone's prostate.
The scene must not be used for diagnosis, treatment or dose selection, prognosis, or planning biopsy, resection, radiotherapy or surgery.

scope: a procedurally built male genital route from testis to external urethral orifice, with the prostate and erectile columns it passes through, bilingual labels and selection behaviour prepared for future clinical sign-off
unresolvedLimitations: Independent medical review of the label set and the Japanese terminology is not yet recorded.
Lengths and calibres are drawn to be legible; the vas deferens in particular is drawn far shorter and straighter than it is.
The epididymis is one tube of three named lengths; the single coiled duct inside it is not modelled and head, body and tail are not separately selectable.
One side of a paired route is drawn.
The scrotum, the spermatic cord's coverings and vessels, the seminiferous tubules, the sphincters, the bulbourethral glands and the erectile mechanism are not drawn, and nothing here changes state.
The prostate here is one undivided translucent gland; its zones are `prostate-anatomy`.
The scene must not be used for diagnosis, treatment or dose selection, prognosis, or planning vasectomy, catheterisation, surgery or any fertility decision.

scope: a procedurally built right knee in extension — bones, articular cartilage, menisci, cruciate and collateral ligaments and the extensor mechanism — with bilingual labels and selection behaviour prepared for future clinical sign-off
unresolvedLimitations: Independent medical review of the label set and the Japanese terminology is not yet recorded.
No length, angle, thickness or attachment footprint is a measurement; bone shapes are simplified solids and cartilage thickness is drawn to be visible.
The joint is drawn at one position, in full extension, and nothing in the scene moves: rolling, gliding and the screw-home rotation are not represented.
Each ligament is one band between two points; the separate bundles of the cruciates and the layers of the medial collateral ligament are not modelled.
The joint capsule, the synovium and its bursae, the popliteus, the posterolateral corner, the hamstring and iliotibial attachments, the meniscal horns, the vessels and the nerves are not drawn.
No injury, degeneration or repair is represented in any form, and nothing here is anyone's knee.
The scene must not be used for diagnosis, treatment or dose selection, prognosis, or planning any injection, arthroscopy, reconstruction or arthroplasty.

scope: a procedurally built right shoulder with the arm at the side — bones, glenoid and labrum, articular cartilage, all four rotator cuff tendons, the long head of biceps and four ligaments — with bilingual labels and selection behaviour prepared for future clinical sign-off
unresolvedLimitations: Independent medical review of the label set and the Japanese terminology is not yet recorded.
No length, angle, thickness or attachment footprint is a measurement; bone shapes are simplified solids and cartilage thickness is drawn to be visible.
The subacromial space is drawn wider than it is, so that the tendon passing under the arch can be seen and selected; it is a display value and no clearance may be read off the model.
The joint is drawn at one position, with the arm at the side, and nothing in the scene moves: the cuff neither tightens nor slackens and the head does not translate.
Each cuff tendon is one strap standing for a muscle and its tendon; the myotendinous junctions and the footprints are not modelled.
The joint capsule apart from one glenohumeral ligament, the subacromial and other bursae, deltoid, the remaining scapular muscles, the vessels and the brachial plexus are not drawn.
Glenoid version and humeral retroversion are not represented.
No tear, impingement, instability or degeneration is represented in any form, and nothing here is anyone's shoulder.
The scene must not be used for diagnosis, treatment or dose selection, prognosis, or planning any injection, arthroscopy, cuff repair, stabilisation or arthroplasty.

scope: a procedurally built right hip, standing — bones, acetabulum and labrum, articular cartilage, the ligament of the head, three capsular ligaments and two tendons — with bilingual labels and selection behaviour prepared for future clinical sign-off

The acetabular notch and transverse ligament, the horseshoe shape of the acetabular cartilage, the bursae, the remaining hip muscles, the retinacular vessels of the head and neck and the sciatic nerve are not drawn.
No fracture, arthritis, impingement, dysplasia or dislocation is represented in any form, and nothing here is anyone's hip.
The scene must not be used for diagnosis, treatment or dose selection, prognosis, or planning any injection, arthroscopy, fixation or arthroplasty.

scope: a procedurally built block of skin — three layers, adipose lobules, a hair follicle with its sebaceous gland, a sweat gland, an arteriole, a venule and a sensory nerve — with bilingual labels and selection behaviour prepared for future clinical sign-off

No rash, ulcer, burn, infection or tumour is represented in any form, and nothing here is anyone’s skin.
The scene must not be used for diagnosis, treatment or dose selection, prognosis, staging a wound, or planning any procedure.

scope: a procedurally built spine — four regions, one lumbar segment in full, the disc, the canal and its contents — with bilingual labels and selection behaviour prepared for future clinical sign-off

Nothing moves or bends: flexion, extension and instability are not represented.
The ribs and their joints, the ligaments of the column, the muscles, the intervertebral foramina as openings, the ligamentum flavum, the epidural fat and venous plexus and the coccyx are not drawn.

scope: Gross anatomy of one nasal cavity and the four paranasal sinuses, and where each sinus and the tear duct open into it. No airflow, no mucociliary clearance, no turbinate swelling, no disease.
unresolvedLimitations: The middle meatus is drawn as a plain gutter: the uncinate process, ethmoid bulla and hiatus semilunaris that actually shape it are not modelled, so the arrangement within the ostiomeatal complex cannot be read off this model.
Only the right cavity, its turbinates and its sinuses are drawn; the left is absent, and no normal variation (deviated septum, absent frontal sinus, concha bullosa) is represented.
The frontal and ethmoid drainage channels are described in the copy and not drawn as geometry.
Nothing swells: the hourly turbinate cycle the copy describes is not animated.

scope: Gross anatomy of the pharynx and larynx and how the airway and the food route are separated. No swallowing, no phonation, no airway movement, no disease, and no procedural route.
unresolvedLimitations: The vocal folds are drawn parted at one fixed display opening (GLOTTIS_DISPLAY_GAP); they neither open, close nor vibrate, and no airway calibre may be read off the gap.
Nothing moves: the soft palate does not lift, the larynx does not rise and the epiglottis does not fold, so the mechanism every structure here exists for is described in the copy and not shown.
The cricothyroid membrane is a landmark only; no route, depth, angle or technique is represented and the scene must not be used to plan one.

The muscles of the larynx and pharynx, the joints between the cartilages, the tongue, the thyroid gland and the lower course of the left recurrent laryngeal nerve are not drawn, and the two nerves are drawn alike where in life they differ.

scope: Gross anatomy of the mouth, the two parts of the tongue and where the three pairs of salivary glands open. No chewing, no swallowing, no tongue movement, no dentition, no disease.
unresolvedLimitations: The jaw is drawn open by a fixed display amount (JAW_DISPLAY_OPENING); it is a position rather than a change of shape, but no opening or occlusal relationship may be read off the model.
Both rows of teeth are drawn as continuous bands following the arch: no individual tooth, root, crown shape, number or eruption stage is represented.

The muscles of the tongue, floor and jaw, the joint of the jaw, and the lingual, hypoglossal and facial nerves are not drawn, so nothing here supports any claim about movement or about the course of a nerve.
The ducts are drawn to the point they open at, not as openings; the vallate papillae are nine standing for eight to twelve, and no other papillae are drawn.

scope: Gross anatomy of the female pelvic floor: what the sheet is attached to, where the gap in it is, what passes through it, and where the sling runs. No contraction, no descent, no pressure, no childbirth, no disease and no procedure.
unresolvedLimitations: The bones are a frame, not a model: there is no iliac wing, no acetabulum and no obturator foramen, and the two hip bones and the symphysis are not separated.
Nothing contracts and nothing descends; the anorectal angle the puborectalis exists to make is drawn at one fixed value that is not a measurement.
The subdivisions of the levator, the fascia and the ligaments that suspend the viscera, the pudendal nerve, the vessels and the internal anal sphincter are not drawn.
Only a female pelvis is drawn, and nothing in the scene supports any claim about childbirth, continence, prolapse or any procedure.

scope: Gross anatomy of the bones of the hand and wrist and of the carpal tunnel and its contents. No joint movement, no tendon excursion, no grip, no blood supply, no disease.
unresolvedLimitations: Bones are smooth blocks and shafts: heads, bases, styloids, joint surfaces, capsules and ligaments are not drawn, and the saddle shape of the thumb’s carpometacarpal joint is described rather than modelled.
The blood supply of the scaphoid — the reason that bone is spoken about the way it is — is not represented at all.

Seven cords stand for the nine flexor tendons and which tendon is which is not represented; the sheaths, the extensor retinaculum and hoods, the thumb’s extensors and the ulnar nerve and artery are not drawn.
No cross-sectional area or pressure is represented, so nothing here supports any claim about the tunnel being narrow enough to matter.

scope: Gross anatomy of the bones of the foot and ankle, the two joints of the hindfoot, and what holds the medial arch up. No weight-bearing, no joint movement, no gait, no blood supply, no disease.
unresolvedLimitations: Nothing bears weight and no joint bends, so the windlass mechanism the copy describes — toe extension tightening the fascia and raising the arch — is described and not shown.

Bones are smooth blocks and shafts: joint surfaces, capsules, the sesamoids, the fat pad under the heel and the tarsal tunnel are not drawn, and the three cuneiforms are drawn as one block so the wedge shape that makes the transverse arch is described rather than shown.
The blood supply of the talus — the reason that bone is spoken about the way it is — is not represented at all.
No ligament strength or order of failure is represented, so nothing here supports any claim about which band tears first beyond what the copy states in words.

scope: How the skeleton is put together: the axial column, the two girdles, and the difference between the two ways a limb is attached. Not the shape of any individual bone, no movement, no weight-bearing, no disease.
unresolvedLimitations: No bone here is a model of that bone: every one is a smooth shaft or block with no joint surfaces, processes, sutures or foramina, and the vertebrae, carpals, tarsals and the bones of the hands and feet are not drawn individually at all.
The figure is one representative adult of no particular sex, age or size; no length, proportion, joint angle or bone count is a measurement.
Nothing moves and nothing bears weight, and cartilage, ligaments, muscle and every soft tissue are absent.
Each structure’s note names the scene that actually models that region, because the detail is deliberately not here.

scope: a geometric model of a urinary tract blocked at one of five named levels: which drawn stretches lie above the blockage, how many kidneys do, and what thickness of parenchyma is left beside a collecting system that has filled inside a capsule that barely yields
unresolvedLimitations: Independent medical review of the five levels, the copy and the Japanese terminology is not yet recorded.
No volume, calibre, thickness or ratio is a measurement. Every one is measured off this repository's own kidney, ureter and bladder builders, whose proportions are drawn to be legible.
The parenchymal thickness is reported against this model's own resting thickness and is not a cortical thickness on any scan. A real kidney thins unevenly; this one thins evenly.
The model contains no kidney function of any kind — no filtration, no creatinine, no urine output, no recovery and no loss — and nothing in it is coupled to renal-filtration.
The model does not grade hydronephrosis. No output is a grade, a stage or a threshold.
There is no cause of the obstruction, no time, no symptom, no infection and no treatment; the axis is how much has backed up rather than how long it has been there.
The obstruction is drawn on the left in every one-sided level because it has to be drawn somewhere; the side carries no claim.
The ureter is drawn as three equal named stretches of one tube so that 'above the blockage' can be said; they are divisions of a drawing and none has a length.
The scene must not be used for diagnosis, treatment or dose selection, or prognosis.

scope: a conservation model of one lobe losing its air: what is left of its volume, how much of the room it vacated the remaining lobes of the same lung take, and how far the midline is drawn across by the remainder
unresolvedLimitations: Independent medical review of the six arrangements, the copy and the Japanese terminology is not yet recorded.
No volume, distance or ratio is a measurement. The lobe shares are this repository's lung atlas's own, and each lobe is reported against its own resting volume.
The midline shift is a volume spread over a face this repository chose. It is not a tracheal deviation, not a mediastinal shift anybody measured, and not millimetres.
How the vacated room divides between the rest of the lung and the hemithorax is a calibration chosen so both halves of the answer are legible; it is not a measured proportion.
The remaining lobes expand in proportion to what each already had. A real lung does not expand evenly, and neither the shape nor the direction of compensatory expansion is claimed.
A fully collapsed lobe is still drawn at an eighth of its volume so that there is something left to point at; that eighth is not a measured residual volume.
The model contains no gas exchange of any kind — no oxygen, shunt, saturation, blood flow or hypoxic vasoconstriction — and says nothing about what anybody's blood is doing.
There is no cause of the obstruction, no time, no breathing cycle, no recovery, no symptom and no treatment.
The model does not grade collapse and does not read a chest radiograph. No output is a sign, a degree or a threshold.
The scene must not be used for diagnosis, treatment or dose selection, or prognosis.

scope: a geometric model of displaced lumbar disc material: how far it has gone along a chosen direction, whether the drawn annulus still closes behind it, and whether the drawn material overlaps the drawn spinal canal or nerve root
unresolvedLimitations: Independent medical review of the three directions, the copy and the Japanese terminology is not yet recorded.
No distance, fraction or state is a measurement. Every distance is measured off this repository’s spine atlas, which declares itself not anatomically validated.
The containment states `intact` and `breached` are NOT the radiological classification. Bulge, protrusion, extrusion and sequestration are defined on measured geometry this model does not have.
Overlap between two drawn shapes is not root contact in anybody, is not a radiological finding, and is not a cause of anything.
The model contains no symptom or sign of any kind. Sciatica, numbness, weakness and reflex change are not outputs and cannot be read off any number here.
The atlas draws one pair of roots at this level, leaving above the disc, so the traversing/exiting root distinction is unavailable and is not claimed.
There is no imaging of any kind: no plane, no sequence, no measurement, and no canal or foraminal stenosis ratio.
There is no time, no cause, no mechanism of injury, no inflammation, no treatment, no natural history and no resorption.
Past the width of what it meets the model stops measuring; it does not push a root aside, deform it, or follow it.
The scene must not be used for diagnosis, treatment or dose selection, or prognosis.

scope: a geometric model of retinal separation as a round patch on the eye atlas’s globe: how far it reaches from a chosen origin, what share of the drawn retina that is, and whether the macula lies inside it
unresolvedLimitations: Independent medical review of the five origins, the copy and the Japanese terminology is not yet recorded.
No angle, area or height is a measurement. The globe, its coats and the macula’s position are this repository’s own eye atlas’s.
The height the retina is drawn lifted is illustrative and much larger than the atlas’s own coat spacing; at the real spacing a separation is a few pixels. It says separated, not how high.
The model contains no vision of any kind and says nothing about what anybody can see.
The model contains no prognosis. Nothing here says what recovers, how much, or whether the macula being inside changes that.
macula-on and macula-off are two pictures, not two stages; nothing says one becomes the other.
There is no cause and no kind: no tear, traction, exudate, myopia or trauma.
There is no time, no fluid, no gravity and no surgery. The inferior origin behaves exactly like the superior one.
The separation is drawn as a circular patch spreading evenly from one point; a real detachment is neither.
The scene must not be used for diagnosis, treatment or dose selection, or prognosis.

scope: a geometric model of lens opacity: which band of the drawn lens has clouded, how much of the drawn pupil that band stands in, and how that share changes with the aperture
unresolvedLimitations: Independent medical review of the three places, the two apertures, the copy and the Japanese terminology is not yet recorded.
No radius, area or fraction is a measurement. The lens and the pupil are this repository’s own eye atlas’s, and both shares are shares of drawn circles.
The share reported is an area inside a drawn aperture. It is not a transmission, not a loss, and not a measure of sight.
The model contains no vision of any kind — no acuity, contrast sensitivity, glare, colour or refraction — and nothing converts its output into any of those.
The model contains no indication for treatment and no output of it is a threshold for one.
There is no light physics: nothing is scattered, refracted or absorbed. A ray either crosses the clouded area or does not.
The two pupil sizes are two apertures, not two light levels; nothing says what made the pupil that size.
The three places are three arrangements, not three stages, and nothing says one becomes another.
Each opacity is an even band at one depth, and the depth is carried for the drawing only; a real opacity is neither even nor confined to a band.
There is no time, no progression and no cause: no age, steroid, diabetes or trauma.
The scene must not be used for diagnosis, treatment or dose selection, or prognosis.

scope: a geometric model of loose particles in a semicircular canal: how much of gravity lies in a chosen canal’s plane for a given head position, where in the loop a particle would settle, and whether that path runs towards the ampulla
unresolvedLimitations: Independent medical review of the two loops, the head’s path, the copy and the Japanese terminology is not yet recorded.
No angle, distance or share is a measurement. The canals’ planes and the loop’s radius are this repository’s own ear atlas’s.
NO EYE MOVEMENT IS DERIVED. Nothing in this model is an eye, a muscle or a direction of gaze, and no output of it is a nystagmus.
There is no symptom, no vertigo, no latency, no duration, no fatigue and no repositioning manoeuvre or its effect.
The model is quasi-static: the particle is drawn where it would end up, with no inertia, no fluid, no drag, no cupula and no time.
The head’s path is one chosen rotation and its extent is a calibration; it is not the angle of any named manoeuvre and no point on the axis is a step of one.

In this drawing the posterior loop answers a turn either way identically, because the atlas draws one ear and the turn is symmetric about that loop’s plane. Only the lateral loop makes the two turns different pictures. That is a property of the drawing.
The particle is drawn as a single body; real otoconia are many, and nothing here says how many or whether they move together.
There is no cause, no recurrence, and nothing about which ear is affected in anybody.
The scene must not be used for diagnosis, treatment or dose selection, or prognosis.

scope: a geometric model of how hard each named depth of a drawn skin block is squeezed under a surface load, over soft tissue and over a bony prominence, and which of those depths takes the most of it
unresolvedLimitations: Independent medical review of the two profiles, the copy and the Japanese terminology is not yet recorded.
No depth, fraction or profile is a measurement. The layer depths are this repository’s skin atlas’s display values, which that atlas declares are deliberately not to scale.
The model does not stage a pressure injury and cannot be made to. No output is a stage, a grade or a threshold, and staging rests on visible tissue and tissue loss that this model does not have.

Deformation here is an unscaled number comparing depths inside one picture. It is not a stress, a strain, a pressure or a displacement, and it may not be compared between the two grounds or between two positions on the axis.
Nothing in the model damages tissue: there is no death, no loss, no ulcer and no wound, and no output converts deformation into an injury.
The two terms of the profile are shapes chosen to be the two shapes, not a mechanics. REACH and TRAPPED are calibrations no one measured; the tests fix the consequence, not the values.
There is no time, no duration and no relief — the axis is how hard the surface is loaded, not how long it has been.
There is no blood, no perfusion, no ischaemia, no inflammation and no repair, and no temperature, moisture, friction or continence.
The bony prominence is a structure the scene adds: the skin atlas is a specimen with no skeleton in it.
There is no person, no body position and no support surface, and nothing here is a risk assessment.
The scene must not be used for diagnosis, treatment or dose selection, or prognosis.

scope: a geometric model of where a place sits in a drawn breast: its position along one of the atlas’s own duct systems or along its axillary tail, which part of that system the position is in, and how far that point is from the drainage route the atlas draws
unresolvedLimitations: Independent medical review of the five places, the copy and the Japanese terminology is not yet recorded.

No distance or position is a measurement. Every course, point and distance is sampled off this repository’s breast atlas, which declares itself not anatomically validated and its duct and lobule counts to be display counts.
Nothing in the model spreads, travels or is carried anywhere. No output is a spread, a nodal status or a risk of either, and the drainage route is drawn because the gland drains that way.
The marker is a place and has no size: no diameter, no volume, no growth, no margin and no shape. It is drawn at one fixed size at every position on every course.
The model produces no stage and no grade. Staging rests on size, on nodes and on what is elsewhere in a person, none of which this model has, and no probability or prognosis is computed.

The part names `large-duct`, `terminal-duct` and `lobular-end` are places on a drawn course. They are NOT histological types and must not be read as ductal or lobular carcinoma or as any classification.
The gland has one drainage route in this picture, the one the atlas draws. A breast has more than one; their absence here is a property of the drawing.

Four of the atlas’s eight duct systems are offered, and the quadrant names say where each happens to point rather than dividing the breast into quadrants. Neither the choice of courses nor the baseline says anything about where lesions occur in people.
There is no biology of any kind: no cell type, no receptor, no histology, no in-situ or invasive distinction and no cause.
There is no imaging, no examination, no screening, no biopsy and no treatment.
The scene must not be used for diagnosis, treatment or dose selection, or prognosis.
